Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for New Zealand's reply. The two umpires and the Sri Lankan players make their way out to the middle. Out walk the Kiwi opening pair of Devon Conway and Rachin Ravindra. Dilshan Madushanka is at the top of his mark and will start the proceedings with the new ball for Sri Lanka. Off we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, the Kiwi bowlers have done their job and it is now upon their batters to finish the job and take them a step closer to the semis. As far as Sri Lanka are concerned, they will need early breakthroughs to stand any chance. Can Dilshan Madushanka and Co. manage to make a match out of this? We will find out when we return in a bit for the chase.

Trent Boult is in for a chat. He says that half the job done and they will now look to chase it down. Adds that the spinners bowled well and it was a lot slower than they expected and hopefully the dew sets in now and they can chase it down quickly. Mentions that it is alwatys a learning curve coming to this part of the world and they have had a couple of tough games and will now look to finish on a high.

As for Sri Lanka, there is not much to write home about except for the contributions from Kusal Perera and Maheesh Theekshana. After being inserted into the bat, it was an 'all or nothing' start from the Sri Lankan batters. Kusal Perera got an early life in Tim Southee's first over, but Pathum Nissanka perished on the very next delivery. It went from bad to worse for Sri Lanka as Kusal Mendis and Sadeera Samarawickrama fell in the space of four deliveries. Despite the fall of wickets at the other end, Perera went about business as usual and registered his fifty off just 22 balls. The centurion from the last game, Charith Asalanka, could not repeat his heroics before the aggressive approach from Perera led to his downfall. Angelo Mathews and Dhananjaya de Silva then got together in an effort to steady the sinking ship, but neither of them had any answers to the guile and control of Mitchell Santner. As he has done in the past few games, Maheesh Theekshana showed stubborn resistance and was prepared to grind it out in the middle. He found an alley in Dilshan Madushanka and thanks to their 43-run stand, Sri Lanka have something to bowl at.

It was Tim Southee who set the tone for New Zealand with a wicket in his first over. His new ball partner, Trent Boult, joined in on the act as well and went bang, bang, in an over to pile more misery on Sri Lanka, getting to 600 international wickets in the process as well. After drawing the first blood, Southee tapered off a bit as he was taken on by Kusal Perera in his next couple of overs. This forced Kane Williamson to bring on Lockie Ferguson, and the speedster did what was asked of him to get rid of the dangerous-looking Perera. After the field restrictions were lifted, Mitchell Santer was introduced, and the master craftsman dented any hopes of a Sri Lankan recovery with twin blows. They were stalled by the gritty knock from Maheesh Theekshana as Kane Williamson kept ringing in changes to pick the final wicket. It was Rachin Ravindra who can do no wrong at this World Cup, as he accounted for Dilshan Madushanka to wrap up the innings. Trent Boult was the pick of the bowlers with three wickets to his name. He also became the 6th bowler to take 50-plus wickets in ODI World Cups. Lockie Ferguson, Mitchell Santner and Rachin Ravindra took two wickets each while Tim Southee had a wicket to his name.

The last-wicket stand finally comes to an end and Sri Lanka have been bowled out for 171! Despite the fight shown by the Sri Lankan tail, this is nowhere close to what they would have set for at the start of the day. The Kiwi bowlers have vindicated their skipper's decision to bowl first, and how. They have certainly taken their game up a notch in what is a must-win game for them.

OUT! EDGED AND GONE! Finally, an extremely gritty stand for the last wicket ends and New Zealand breathe a sigh of relief. Rachin Ravindra drifts this one in beautifully onto middle stump and gets it to dip nicely. Dilshan Madushanka is caught on the back foot and tries to block it out but the ball grips and turns away, taking a faint outside edge and the ball is gobbled up by Tom Latham behind the sticks. Sri Lanka are bowled out for 171!

Commentary.Commentary: Done and dusted with the pre-match formalities and it is now time to play! The two umpires are out in the middle and the Kiwi players have taken their places on the field as well. Kusal Perera will open the innings for Sri Lanka alongside Pathum Nissanka. We are just a few minutes away from the start of this crucial game. But first, the two sets of players along with their mascots will line up for their respective national anthems. It will be the national anthem of Sri Lanka first, followed by the national anthem of New Zealand.

Sri Lanka's skipper Kusal Mendis says that they wanted to bowl first but adds that it is not much of a worry. Feels that the wicket looks good and they will look to play good cricket and put a good total on the board. Mentions that it is a very important game in the context of the Champions Trophy berth. Adds that they need to do the basics right and stick to the team's plans. Shares that New Zealand is a much calmer team as compared to their last opponent. Reckons that they played well here in the last game against England where the bowlers bowled well. Informs that Chamika Karunaratne comes into the side in place of Kasun Rajitha.

Kane Williamson, the captain of New Zealand says they will have a bowl first due to the inclement weather and will look to make use of the conditions early on. Adds that they have won a few and lost a few but have been able to play the way they want to. Mentions that there were so many factors to the losses and some of them were really close losses and will look to focus on this game and get the job done. Informs that Lockie Ferguson comes in for Ish Sodhi and that is a decision made according to the pitch which looks a bit different to the previous one here.

PITCH REPORT - Mark Howard is pitchside. He says there have been heavy thunderstorms in the last few days over here but the chance of rain is not much today. Adds that 73m straight is the longest hit and the square boundaries aren't big. Sanjay Manjrekar joins him and says that the pitch is exactly like the previous ones here and it is a batting paradise. Adds that the pace reduction is the least here and hence, the batters can score more and hit more sixes. Manjrekar reckons that considering the weather and the conditions, both captains might think to chase.

On the flip side, it has been a dismal campaign for the 1996 winners, Sri Lanka. With them out of semi-final contention at the World Cup, there is still a Champions Trophy berth to play for Kusal Mendis and Co. They are coming off a loss against Bangladesh, and it was one to forget, especially for Angelo Mathews for that timed-out incident. Sadeera Samarawickrama and Kusal Mendis have been their batting mainstays, but the Sri Lankan think tank will be happy with the way Charith Asalanka stepped up to score a century in the last game. Dilshan Madushanka has been their find of the tournament, but a lack of support for him has been a cause for concern. Will Sri Lanka manage to deny New Zealand the two points? Or will rain have the final say? We will find out soon. Toss and team news coming up shortly...

It has been a tale of two halves for New Zealand, who started the World Cup with four wins on the trot before losing four games on the bounce. The Kiwis are still the best-placed team to make it to the semis courtesy of their NRR, which is the best among the three teams in contention. Their last outing against Pakistan marked the return of skipper Kane Williamson, who performed as if he never left to provide a much-needed boost to their batting. Ever since the opening night, Devon Conway has struggled for runs, but it has been more than made up for by young sensation Rachin Ravindra's purple patch. Trent Boult was uncharacteristically expensive, as was Ish Sodhi, but expect them to pull their socks up in this all-important game.

Hello and a warm welcome, ladies and gentlemen! Match number 41 of the 2023 ODI World Cup is upon us, which sees New Zealand go up against Sri Lanka at the M.Chinnaswamy Stadium in Bengaluru. With only one semi-final spot up for grabs, this is a crunch game for New Zealand, as a win here will take them one step closer to the semis. A lot is riding on this game for Pakistan and Afghanistan as well, who will be hoping for a New Zealand defeat, which will make their job a little bit easier. The weather is iffy, and if this fixture gets washed out, it will favour the two Asian sides.
